method_definition: GLM-5.3 at the official low reasoning effort through the GLM Coding Plan OpenCode integration generates Blender Python scene code; fixed Blender construction and rendering; procedural geometry and materials, no external scene assets
api_seed_note: Logical seeds index fresh independent Claude Code sessions. The service does not expose a deterministic sampling seed; preserve generated.py for deterministic local reconstruction.
notes: The API key is supplied only through the GLM53_API_KEY process environment and is never written to manifests, commands, logs, or repository files.
Every request uses the exact OpenCode provider/model identifier glm-coding-plan/glm-5.3 and records OpenCode JSON events plus the returned session identifier and token usage.
The installed OpenCode 1.1.1 is isolated under baselines/methods/glm_flash/runtime/glm53_opencode and uses the official OpenAI-compatible Coding Plan endpoint.
The first exploratory queue was preserved under data/glm_5_3_pilot. It exposed the Claude Code 32000-token ceiling before protocol freeze; no exploratory output enters the formal matrix.

Pilot v2 was preserved and excluded: requesting 65536 output tokens does not override Claude Code 2.0.62's 32000-token custom-model cap, and default maximum reasoning produced an unresolved three-attempt infrastructure failure.

Pilot v3 was preserved and excluded: Claude Code 2.0.62 did not transmit its configured low effort, so GLM-5.3 remained at the default max effort and repeatedly exceeded that client's 32000-token cap.
Pilot v4 was preserved and excluded: MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 merely omitted the Anthropic thinking field, while GLM-5.3 defaults to max and does not support disabling thinking.

The uniform v5 pilot and formal method use the official glm-5.3 model code with thinking enabled and reasoning_effort low. OpenCode title generation is disabled with an explicit title and all agent tools are disabled so each slot issues exactly one main-model request.

Before formal freeze, the v5 pilot acceptance gate was set to at least one fully rendered valid scene per domain: its purpose is end-to-end interface and metric validation, while every formal quality failure remains an ITT lower-bound result without replacement or resampling.
Unstarted slots are missing data, not ITT failures. Only terminal preregistered quality failures receive ITT lower bounds.
Shared frozen Table-2 renderer, cameras, metric environments, caches, specs and seeds are reused without modifying another method's artifacts.
